_note: Evolution itself, made a fixture (local-ai-engine.md §4.2 rules 1-2, §4.4). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) SELF-DESCRIPTION — `despia_ai_capabilities()` reports what THIS build carries (engines, formats, modalities, tool dialects, features, limits), and every consumer ADAPTS to the reported surface instead of hardcoding it. A consumer that assumes `gbnf` exists fails on a build without it; a consumer that asks, degrades. (2) ADDITIVE EVOLUTION — every JSON envelope carries a `schema_version` and unknown fields are MUST-IGNORE in both directions, so a newer catalog served to an older runtime does not crash it. (3) An entry the runtime cannot serve is SKIPPED with typed absence, never a parse failure that takes the whole catalog with it — one bad or too-new row must never blind an app to the rest of its models. (4) Retirement is not a kill switch: a `retired` entry stops NEW downloads while an already-installed model keeps working forever, because 'you own your OWN AI' is enforced here or it is marketing. (5) Unknown capability keys reported by a NEWER engine are ignored by an older consumer for the same reason, in the same direction.

cases.name: capabilities: consumers adapt to the reported surface
cases._note: Two builds, one catalog, different answers. The build without `gbnf` cannot serve an entry that requires it, and says so rather than trying and failing at generate time.

cases.name: capabilities: the same catalog on a richer build serves the entry
cases._note: The mirror image of the previous case — nothing about the catalog changed, only what the build reports.

cases.name: capabilities: a newer catalog schema_version is tolerated, not fatal
cases._note: Fleets straddle releases. A catalog written for a newer runtime carries fields this one has never heard of; the known rows still load, the unknown FIELDS are ignored, and the app keeps working.

cases.name: capabilities: an entry requiring a newer ABI is skipped, the rest load
cases._note: The containment assertion. One future row must not blind the app to its working models: the unservable entry is skipped with a typed reason and every other row is unaffected.

cases.name: capabilities: a malformed entry is skipped and the catalog still loads
cases._note: Hostile or broken data is a row-level problem. A row missing its id or its engine is dropped with a notice; the catalog is not a transaction that fails whole.

cases.name: capabilities: retirement blocks new downloads and never disables an installed model
cases._note: The no-kill-switch law, in one case. `old` is retired upstream: it disappears from what can be downloaded and still answers when asked to run, because it is already on the user's device and the user owns it.

cases.name: capabilities: a deprecated entry still downloads and warns
cases._note: Deprecation is a signal, not a wall — the row stays downloadable and carries its status so a dashboard can nudge, which is the whole difference between deprecated and retired.

cases.name: capabilities: unknown reported capability keys are ignored by an older consumer
cases._note: Must-ignore in the other direction: a newer engine reporting surfaces this consumer has never heard of changes nothing about how it behaves.
